results.content:
# Reproducing the run

## Environment

Use the image (`Dockerfile`, built on `radixark/miles:dev`): Megatron-LM, SGLang,
TransformerEngine, Ray and the HF→Megatron converter come preinstalled and the two
frameworks are symlinked to `Megatron-LM/` and `sglang/` in the repo root, which is what
`justrl2/train.sh` expects. Mount `models/`, `datasets/` and `runs/` from the host.
Without the image, see `third_party/README.md`.

Inside the container:

```bash
bash   justrl2/prepare_model.sh     # openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model -> models/ (+ torch_dist), needs 1 GPU
python justrl2/prepare_data.py      # openbmb/UltraData-RL-2609 (Math) -> datasets/
```

Model: <https://huggingface.co/openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model> ·
Data: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/openbmb/UltraData-RL-2609/tree/main/data/Math>

## Hardware and topology

The reference run used 16 nodes × 8 H100: 8 actor nodes + 8 critic nodes, SGLang engines
colocated on all GPUs, TP 1 / CP 4, global batch 480 (60 prompts × 8 samples).

PPO in miles requires **actor world size == critic world size** (the actor↔critic NCCL
groups are built rank-pairwise). `justrl2/train.sh` defaults to `WORLD_SIZE/2` nodes each
and refuses to start otherwise. The global batch must be divisible by the actor data
parallel size (`nodes × gpus / TP / CP`); with the defaults that is 480 / 16 — fine.

`justrl2/configs/debug-1node-8gpu.env` splits one node 4 + 4 for a pipeline smoke test.
The reference run never used a single node, so treat that config as untested plumbing,
not as a small-scale recipe.

## Launch

On every node (Ray head is `RANK=0`; `MASTER_ADDR`/`MASTER_PORT`/`WORLD_SIZE`/`RANK` must be
set by your scheduler, or left unset for a single node):

```bash
bash justrl2/train.sh justrl2/configs/minicpm5-2b-math-128k.env
```

Override any knob through the environment, e.g. `GAE_LAMBDA_K=0.4 CRITIC_VALUE_BIAS_INIT=0.5`.
Extra arguments after the config are passed straight to `train.py`.

### Startup checks worth reading

- `[critic-value-head] ... after-load ... w_absmax=0.189` then
  `re-zeroed [...] (bias_init=0.52, master params resynced)` — the post-load re-init ran.
- The first rollout's sample responses are coherent text. If they are garbage,
  `MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH` points at an `iter_xxx` subdirectory instead of its parent and
  Megatron silently started from random weights.
- `critic exclude shaping: critic returns computed from rewards without overlong penalty`.

### Resume

Re-run the same command. Actor and critic checkpoints under `SAVE_ROOT/EXP_TAG` and
`SAVE_ROOT/EXP_TAG_critic` are loaded automatically; a half-present pair is a hard error.
If you changed `NUM_ROLLOUT`, add `OVERRIDE_OPT_PARAM_SCHEDULER=1` on the first resume.

## Evaluate

The reference run set `EVAL_INTERVAL=1000` (no in-training eval) and evaluated the HF
exports (`SAVE_ROOT/EXP_TAG/hf/iter_XXXXXXX`, every 5 steps) offline:

```bash
python justrl2/eval.py --model runs/<EXP_TAG>/hf/iter_0000299 \
    --data datasets/aime-2025.jsonl --data datasets/aime-2026.jsonl \
    --n 16 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 126976
```

Reports acc@16, pass@16, mean length and truncation rate per file. AIME differences of
1–2 problems are within noise at n = 16; compare peaks over a window, not single points.

## What the original internal run did differently

Two knobs in the released config are refinements over what that run literally executed:

| | original run | released config |
|---|---|---|
| value-head bias init | 0 | `CRITIC_VALUE_BIAS_INIT=0.52` (validated in a separate arm with 0.5: +0.022 AIME over the shared 120-step window, warmup transient removed) |
| GAE λ | `1 − 1/(α·L)`, α = 1.5 (≡ k ≈ 0.513) | `k^(1/L)`, `GAE_LAMBDA_K=0.5` — same functional form, k rounded from 0.513 to 0.5 |

To reproduce the original literally: `CRITIC_VALUE_BIAS_INIT=0 GAE_LAMBDA_K=0.513`. Everything else
(rollout sizes, clip, warmup, overlong penalty, `CRITIC_EXCLUDE_OLP=1`, LR, dynamic
sampling, partial rollout) is as run; DSpark speculative decoding, which that run used
for rollout speed, is unavailable in the community SGLang build (see
`third_party/README.md`) and does not change the recipe.

## Determinism

Bitwise reproduction needs SGLang deterministic inference + Megatron deterministic mode
(`--sglang-enable-deterministic-inference --sglang-attention-backend flashinfer
--deterministic-mode`, plus `NCCL_ALGO=Ring NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` in the Ray runtime env) and uninstalling flash-attn 3.
It is slower; the reference numbers were not produced this way.
=====METHOD=====
# JustRL2 — the method

JustRL2 is PPO for long-context (128k) math reasoning with a **separate critic that has no
language-model head**, a **mean-reward-seeded value head**, and a **length-adaptive GAE λ**.
This page explains each piece and points at the code; the full write-up with experiments
and ablations is the blog post [JustRL-II: Scaling Small LLMs to 128k Reasoning with a
Critic](https://panhaoxuan.notion.site/justrl-ii-scaling-small-llms-to-128k-reasoning-with-a-critic)
([中文](https://panhaoxuan.notion.site/justrl-ii-small-llms-to-128k-reasoning-with-a-critic-cn)). File paths are relative to the repo
root; the framework is [Miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) (SGLang rollout +
Megatron-LM training).

## 1. cc-noLM critic: a scalar value head instead of an LM head

The critic is a second copy of the policy architecture whose `output_layer` is replaced by
`LinearForLastLayer(input_size=hidden, output_size=1)` —
[`miles/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py`](../miles/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py).
It emits one scalar `V` per token and is trained only on the value loss; there is no
token-prediction loss on the critic at all. Keeping the `[vocab, hidden]` LM head around
was the source of the pollution bug in §2, and it costs memory for nothing.

The critic runs as its own Ray training group with the same world size as the actor
(`--critic-num-nodes == --actor-num-nodes`; NCCL groups are built rank-pairwise), colocated
with the SGLang engines.

## 2. Value-head init: zero weight, bias = expected mean reward — re-applied after load

**Construction.** For the scalar head the weight is zero-initialised and the bias is filled
with `--critic-value-bias-init` (0.52 in the released config; the ablation that measured the
effect used 0.5 — see docs/reproduce.md). With a zero weight, `V ≡ bias`
at step 0, so the bias *is* the critic's prior.

Why not the usual `N(0, 0.02)` weight: on a 2048-wide hidden state that gives
`std(V) ≈ 0.02·√H·rms(h) ≈ 9.7` against targets in `[0, 1]`. Why not a zero bias: the value
loss then opens at `E[r²] ≈ 0.5` with a first critic gradient norm of 130–140, and the head
spends its first ~25 steps learning the offset *while the policy already updates against it*.
Seeded at the mean reward the loss opens at `Var(r) ≈ 0.25` and the gradient norm stays
under 40 from step 0 — the transient is gone at zero cost (blog, value-head-init figure).

**After loading the base checkpoint.** The critic starts from the policy/base checkpoint.
Megatron's dist-ckpt reader fills the `[1, H]` head from the overlapping region of the
`[vocab, H]` LM head (measured `w_absmax 0.189`, i.e. `V ~ ±8`) and the load path resets the
bias. `_rezero_critic_value_head` in
[`miles/backends/megatron_utils/checkpoint.py`](../miles/backends/megatron_utils/checkpoint.py)
therefore runs after every finetune-style load: it zeroes the weight again, **re-fills the
bias** with the same value, and calls `optimizer.reload_model_params()` so the fp32 master
copy matches (otherwise the first optimizer step would restore the polluted values).
On resume (`finetune=False`) it does nothing — the trained head from the critic's own
checkpoint is kept.

Verify at startup:
```
[critic-value-head] re-zeroed ['...output_layer.weight', '...output_layer.bias'] after policy-ckpt load (bias_init=0.52, master params resynced)
```
If you port this to another trainer and skip the post-load step, the run is silently broken.

## 3. Length-adaptive GAE: λ_i = k^(1/L_i), returns at λ = 1

`get_advantages_and_returns_batch` in
[`miles/utils/ppo_utils.py`](../miles/utils/ppo_utils.py) computes a per-sample λ from
`length_adaptive_lambda`:

```
λ_i = k ^ (1 / L_i)          (L_i = response length, k = --gae-lambda-k)
```

With γ = 1 the GAE weight of the terminal reward at the first token is `λ_i^(L_i-1)` (the
terminal reward enters δ at the last step), so this choice makes it `k^(1-1/L_i)` — constant
in length up to the O(1/L) correction: the fraction of terminal credit that reaches
the beginning of the response is a constant instead of decaying with length. Longer responses
get a λ closer to 1, so credit propagation does not weaken on 100k-token solutions.

Two details:

- **Decoupled targets.** The *advantage* uses `λ_i`; the *value target* (`returns`) is the
  λ = 1 suffix-reward sum. The critic regresses an unbiased return while the advantage uses
  the length-adaptive discount. This requires γ = 1 (asserted).
- **fp32.** At 128k, `λ = 1 − O(1e-5)`, which bf16 rounds to exactly 1.0; λ is computed in
  fp32 and only cast when handed to the GAE scan.

`k = 0.5` is the release value: half of the terminal credit reaches the first token. The

`LinearForLastLayer(input_size=hidden, output_size=1)` —

(`--critic-num-nodes == --actor-num-nodes`; NCCL groups are built rank-pairwise), colocated
with the SGLang engines.

`std(V) ≈ 0.02·√H·rms(h) ≈ 9.7` against targets in `[0, 1]`. Why not a zero bias: the value
loss then opens at `E[r²] ≈ 0.5` with a first critic gradient norm of 130–140, and the head
spends its first ~25 steps learning the offset *while the policy already updates against it*.
Seeded at the mean reward the loss opens at `Var(r) ≈ 0.25` and the gradient norm stays
under 40 from step 0 — the transient is gone at zero cost (blog, value-head-init figure).

name: analyze-training-crash
description: Analyze Miles training crashes and instability using logs, metrics, train-inference mismatch signals, IcePop/R3 configuration, entropy, grad_norm, response_length, truncated_ratio, reward, dynamic sampling, and SGLang/Ray/Megatron failure evidence.
---

# Analyze Training Crash

## Triage Goal

Use this skill when a Miles training task crashes, diverges, hangs, OOMs, or becomes unstable. Start from evidence, then decide whether the issue is:

- Infrastructure/runtime: Ray, SGLang, NCCL, CUDA, process death, OOM.
- Configuration mismatch: model args, checkpoint, TP/CP/EP, context length, tokenizer/chat template.
- Train-inference mismatch: rollout distribution differs too much from actor training distribution.
- RL instability: reward variance, entropy collapse/spike, grad norm spike, excessive truncation, bad dynamic sampling.
- Task implementation bug: reward, multi-turn parser, tool execution, dataset schema, or prompt formatting.

## Missing Inputs

If the user only says the run crashed or is unstable, ask for the missing evidence before diagnosing. Required inputs:

- Launch script or exact command, including runtime env overrides.
- Error logs around the first failure, not only the final stack trace.
- Optional: screenshots of TensorBoard/WandB or other metric dashboards around the failure.

If some inputs are unavailable, ask for the smallest useful subset first: launch script, first error log, and metric snapshot near the failing step. Do not claim a root cause without at least one concrete log, metric, or config signal.

## Gather Evidence

Collect these before changing code:

- Full launch script and runtime env overrides.
- Ray job logs and actor/rollout logs.
- SGLang logs around the first error.
- TensorBoard/WandB metrics around the first abnormal step.
- Checkpoint iteration, HF checkpoint path, and Megatron `--load` path.
- Recent changes to reward, generate function, tool execution, model args, or data.

If there are many logs, search first for `Traceback`, `ERROR`, `OOM`, `CUDA out of memory`, `NCCL`, `NaN`, `inf`, `timeout`, `Killed`, `router`, `routing`, `truncated`, and `reward`.

## Train-Inference Mismatch

Check whether rollout and training behavior diverged too much:

- Was IcePop/TIS enabled?
  - `--use-tis`
  - `--custom-tis-function-path miles.backends.training_utils.loss.icepop_function`
  - reasonable `--tis-clip-low` and `--tis-clip`
- For MoE, was R3/routing replay enabled?
  - `--use-rollout-routing-replay`
  - `--use-miles-router`
- Did routed expert settings change between rollout and actor?
- Did SGLang use a different tokenizer, chat template, context length, dtype, or MoE fusion behavior from training?
- Did the checkpoint loaded by actor match the HF checkpoint used by rollout?

For MiniCPM5 `16a3b`, suspect train-inference mismatch early if routing replay/R3 is missing or SGLang MoE settings differ from the existing scripts.

## Metric Checks

Inspect metrics around the first bad step, not only the final crash:

- `entropy`: collapse can indicate over-confident policy or bad reward pressure; sudden spike can indicate distribution shift.
- `grad_norm`: spikes often precede NaN/inf, optimizer instability, bad batches, or too-large effective batch changes.
- `response_length`: sudden growth may cause memory pressure, truncation, or reward hacking.
- `truncated_ratio`: high or rising values mean `ROLLOUT_MAX_RESPONSE_LEN`/context length is too small or the policy is running away.
- reward mean/std/nonzero ratio: zero std breaks GRPO usefulness; high variance may destabilize training.
- KL/TIS/ratio metrics: clipping saturation can indicate train-inference mismatch or stale logprobs.
- tokens per GPU and dynamic batch metrics: spikes can explain OOMs or slow/hung steps.

Do not treat the crash stack alone as the root cause if metrics degraded earlier.

## Logs to Interpret

Common patterns:

- CUDA OOM during rollout: reduce `SGLANG_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS`, `SGLANG_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS`, context length, response length, or memory fraction.
- CUDA OOM during training/logprobs: reduce `MAX_TOKENS_PER_GPU`, `LOGPROBS_MAX_TOKENS_PER_GPU`, batch size, or increase recompute.
- NCCL timeout/hang: check dead ranks, OOM before timeout, TP/CP/EP mismatch, and per-rank divergence.
- Reward import failure: verify `--custom-rm-path`, `PYTHONPATH`, and function signature.
- Multi-turn parser/tool errors: verify `--generate-tool-call-parser`, tool specs, tool key, sandbox dependencies, and truncation.
- Checkpoint load failure: verify model args, `--hf-checkpoint`, `--load`, `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt`, and iteration directory.

## Recommended Stabilizing Configuration

When instability is not yet diagnosed, compare the run to these defaults:

- Use IcePop/TIS for train-inference correction.
- For MoE, enable R3/routing replay through Miles Router.
- Enable dynamic sampling:
  - `--over-sampling-batch-size`
  - `--dynamic-sampling-filter-path miles.rollout.filter_hub.dynamic_sampling_filters.check_reward_nonzero_std`
- Keep GRPO conservative at first: low/zero entropy coef, clipped ratios, and existing script defaults.
- For long or agent tasks, lower rollout concurrency before changing algorithmic behavior.

These are recommended defaults, not proof of root cause. Confirm with metrics and logs.

## Analysis Output

When reporting back, use this structure:

1. Symptom: what failed and at which step/component.
2. Most likely root cause: one concise hypothesis backed by evidence.
3. Supporting signals: metrics/log lines/config comparisons.
4. Fix: smallest change to test first.
5. Follow-up checks: metrics to watch in the next run.

Avoid vague conclusions such as "training is unstable" without naming the first abnormal metric or log evidence.

Environment variables (optional): `SWANLAB_API_KEY`, `SWANLAB_LOG_DIR`, `SWANLAB_MODE`

results.content:
# Long-Context RL Training Strategy Research

## Objective
Run MiniCPM5 MoE RL training with rollout-max-response-len=62000 on 8x H100 80GB without OOM, while achieving raw_reward growth.

## Model Architecture
- MiniCPM5 MoE: hidden=1280, 20 layers, 160 experts (top-16), EP=8
- max_position_embeddings: 65536
- Per-GPU memory: ~2 GB model weights (with EP=8), ~10 GB optimizer states

## Problem Analysis

### Original Template Command
The template uses CP=2, max-tokens-per-gpu=16384, rollout-max-response-len=62000. With CP=2, a 63K-token sample becomes ~31.5K per GPU, exceeding the 16384 limit.

### Root Causes of Failure
1. **Truncation + Routing Replay Bug**: truncate_oversized_samples modifies total_lengths metadata but the routing replay tensor retains pre-truncation concatenated size, causing split_with_sizes RuntimeError.
2. **No Activation Recomputation**: Without --recompute-granularity full, all 20 layers activations are stored during backward, consuming extra memory.
3. **No Loss Recomputation**: Output layer logits [T, V] = [16K, 130K] consume ~8.5 GB per microbatch.

## Solution Strategy

Set max_tokens_per_gpu * cp_size >= rollout_max_context_len so no sample exceeds the effective microbatch token budget. This eliminates truncation entirely.

### Working Configuration (Config 2)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| context-parallel-size | 4 |
| max-tokens-per-gpu | 16384 |
| Effective limit | 65536 (>= max sample 63024) |
| n-samples-per-prompt | 8 |
| global-batch-size | 64 |
| rollout-max-context-len | 65536 |
| recompute-granularity | full (uniform, 1 layer) |
| recompute-loss-function | yes |
| sglang-mem-fraction | 0.55 |
| log-probs-chunk-size | 4096 |

## Experimental Results

### Config 1 (CP=4, n_samples=4, 2 rollouts)

| Metric | Rollout 0 | Rollout 1 |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| raw_reward | 0.688 | 0.594 |
| response_len (mean) | 20943 | 20699 |
| response_len (max) | 62000 | 62000 |
| truncated_ratio | 9.4% | 9.4% |
| Training peak allocated | 42.16 GB | - |
| Training peak reserved | 61.87 GB | - |

### Config 2 (CP=4, n_samples=8, 3 rollouts)

| Metric | Rollout 0 | Rollout 1 | Rollout 2 |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| raw_reward | 0.672 | 0.547 | 0.578 |
| response_len (mean) | 19753 | 23963 | 20366 |
| truncated_ratio | 6.3% | 15.6% | 10.9% |
| Training peak allocated | 42.17 GB | - | - |
| Training peak reserved | 62.45 GB | - | - |

Both configs completed without OOM. Peak memory ~42 GB allocated, ~62 GB reserved. Headroom: ~17 GB on the tightest rank.

## Key Findings

### 1. Training Fits in 80 GB with CP=4 + Recompute
Peak allocated ~42 GB (52% of 80 GB), peak reserved ~62 GB (78%).

### 2. Truncation Bug with Routing Replay
Fixed by skipping truncation when rollout_max_context_len <= effective_limit.

### 3. GRPO Zero-Advantage Problem
rewards ~ 0 and pg_loss ~ 0 even with n_samples=8 because GRPO normalizes within each prompt group. When all samples get the same binary reward, the normalized advantage is 0 and the model receives no gradient signal.

### 4. TorchMemorySaver Incompatibility
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True is incompatible with TorchMemorySaver (used for colocated offloading). Must not be set.

## Recommendations for raw_reward Growth
1. Increase n_samples_per_prompt to 16+ for more variance within groups
2. Use harder math problems (target ~50% success rate)
3. Use continuous rewards instead of binary
4. Reduce rollout-max-response-len to prevent 62K cap hits
5. Tune temperature for output diversity

## Usage
```bash
NUM_ROLLOUT=10 bash scripts/community/run-longcontext-research.sh --config 2 \
  --hf-checkpoint /path/to/model \
  --load /path/to/megatron_ckpt \
  --save /path/to/save
```

steps.message:
`. The judge receives the full CoT. But `extract_non_reasoning_content` also applies to `reference = sample.label`; labels are answers without tags, fine. The judge sees `[STUDENT ANSWER] reasoning... final`. The judge's instruction: "First write EXACTLY ONE short sentence stating what final result the STUDENT ANSWER actually asserts." A long CoT may assert several results. It will likely pick the final one. If the final answer is wrong, the judge says NO. So the reward isn't necessarily inflated. But the failure mode is that the policy can place the correct answer anywhere and the judge may accept it. During RL, the policy will discover phrasings that make the judge say YES, e.g., ending the CoT with "The answer is X" before writing the actual final answer (or not). This is a reward-hacking channel.

Even more concretely: with the model's CoT prefilled and truncated before final answer (early 14-18%), the judge sees only reasoning. If the reasoning contains "the answer is 70" as an intermediate conclusion, the judge may accept it. The missing truncation gate makes those samples rewardable. That's a direct reward-hacking gradient to put the answer in the CoT and never finish.

But how do we see it in the observed metrics? Early truncation 14-18% with reward 0.32-0.39; later truncation ~1% with reward 0.62. If truncated samples were getting YES from CoT mentions, reward would be higher at early steps, not lower. Hmm. Unless the early truncated CoTs often don't contain the final answer. The observed pattern actually suggests truncated samples get low reward, and as truncation decreases, reward increases. That's a benign story.

Alternative: The reward increase might come from the model learning to emit the answer earlier/more often. Still benign.

What evidence do we have that the reward is fake? Only the code path. The task says "Do not assume that an unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior." So I need to connect the strip failure to the *observed behavior*: `rollout/raw_reward` (the mean judge score) rises, and the only change in the reward input distribution is that the judge sees the full CoT. But we can't see the counterfactual.

Maybe there is a subtle quantitative signature: the model's true accuracy on `simple-math` should be high; the judge reward 0.62. Hmm.

Wait — maybe the metrics include `raw_reward` at step 0 = 0.3887, which is the *base model's* judge score on simple-math with CoT visible. If the base model (JustRL-II base) scores 61% on AIME 2025 (much harder than simple-math), its simple-math accuracy should be >90%, not 39%. But the run's base model is a "fusion_think" MiniCPM5-2.6B, not necessarily the JustRL-II base. The monitoring doc says raw_reward trending up is healthy. So the training-side picture looks healthy. The defect is in what the reward measures. This supports the "deceptive health" narrative.

Also note "GRPO Zero-Advantage Problem": rewards ~0 and pg_loss ~0 because GRPO normalizes within each prompt group. That explains why `rollout/rewards` is 0.0 in the log and why `advantages` are near zero. Wait — `rollout/rewards` is the *centered* reward, so mean 0.0. The doc says "rewards ~ 0 and pg_loss ~ 0 even with n_samples=8 because GRPO normalizes within each prompt group." That's exactly the explanation. Good.

But there's a subtlety: `rollout/advantages` in our metrics is near zero at most steps, with 145 nonzero. Could that indicate a training signal issue (zero advantage / no gradient)? If most groups have zero variance, dynamic sampling should drop them; but maybe the dynamic sampling filter isn't effective or `rewards_normalization` isn't applied. Let's look at the actual `advantages` distribution more: most values ~1e-9 (float noise), so the logged `rollout/advantages` is probably the mean advantage over samples (which is exactly 0 by construction). With per-token weighting, it's a weighted mean not exactly 0; 145 nonzero are those with unequal token counts. So it's not a defect. Good.

import asyncio
import logging
import time

import ray

from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH, GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE, GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS

from miles.ray.placement_group import create_placement_groups, create_rollout_manager, create_training_models
from miles.utils.arguments import parse_args
from miles.utils.async_utils import eager_create_task
from miles.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger
from miles.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action
from miles.utils.tracking_utils import finish_tracking, init_tracking

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _vram_phase(rollout_id: int, phase: str):
    logger.info(f"===== VRAM-Phase rollout={rollout_id} phase={phase} t={time.time():.1f} =====")


async def train(args):
    configure_logger()
    # allocate the GPUs
    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
    init_tracking(args)

    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])

    # create the actor and critic models
    actor_model, critic_model = await create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)

    if args.offload_rollout:
        await rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote()

    # always update weight first so that sglang has the loaded weights from training.
    await actor_model.update_weights()

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        await rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="compare")

    if args.offload_rollout:
        await rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote()

    # special case for eval-only
    if args.num_rollout == 0 and args.eval_interval is not None:
        await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id=0)

    async def offload_train():
        if args.offload_train:
            if args.use_critic:
                await critic_model.offload()
                if rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps:
                    await actor_model.offload()
            else:
                await actor_model.offload()
        else:
            await actor_model.clear_memory()

    async def save(rollout_id):
        if (not args.use_critic) or (rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps):
            await actor_model.save_model(
                rollout_id,
                force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
            )
        if args.use_critic:
            await critic_model.save_model(
                rollout_id,
                force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
            )
        if args.rollout_global_dataset:
            await rollout_manager.save.remote(rollout_id)

    consecutive_high_no_grad = 0

    # train loop.
    # note that for async training, one can change the position of the sync operation(ray.get).
    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
        if args.eval_interval is not None and rollout_id == 0 and not args.skip_eval_before_train:
            await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id)

        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "generate_start")
        rollout_data_ref = await rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id)
        rollout_metrics = await rollout_manager.get_latest_rollout_metrics.remote()
        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "generate_end")

        no_grad = rollout_metrics.get("grpo_metrics/no_grad")
        if args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold is not None:
            if no_grad is None:
                consecutive_high_no_grad = 0
            elif no_grad > args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold:
                consecutive_high_no_grad += 1
                logger.warning(
                    "rollout %s grpo_metrics/no_grad=%.4f exceeded threshold %.4f (%s/%s)",
                    rollout_id,
                    no_grad,
                    args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold,
                    consecutive_high_no_grad,
                    args.stop_on_no_grad_patience,
                )
                if consecutive_high_no_grad >= args.stop_on_no_grad_patience:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Stopping early before actor update because no_grad stayed above threshold for %s rollouts",
                        consecutive_high_no_grad,
                    )
                    break
            else:
                consecutive_high_no_grad = 0

        if args.offload_rollout:
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "offload_rollout_start")
            offload_tags = [GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH]
            if "kv_cache" in args.offload_rollout_level:
                offload_tags.append(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE)
            if "weight" in args.offload_rollout_level:
                offload_tags.append(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS)
            await rollout_manager.offload.remote(tags=offload_tags)

---

# Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The run's only training signal is an LLM-judge reward that is computed on the model's raw chain-of-thought, not on its final answer. The run appears healthy only because the corrupted reward rises; the snapshot contains no held-out evaluation that could contradict it.

## Root causes

**1. The thinking-strip is a no-op under the effective chat template, so the judge sees the entire CoT.**
- `outputs/launch_command.txt` appends `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'` (and `--rm-type llm_judge_equiv`) after the script, overriding the script's `{"enable_thinking": false}` (`scripts/minicpm5/2_6b/short_rl/run-minicpm5-26b-short-math-8k-colocate.sh:121`) and `--rm-type math` (`:136`).
- `model/chat_template.jinja:168-176`: when `add_generation_prompt=True` and `enable_thinking is true`, the rendered prompt ends with `<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n`. (I rendered the template; the tail is exactly that. With `false`, it ends with `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`.)
- `miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:244-245` sets `sample.response` from SGLang's generated text only, so the prompt's `<think>` is not in the response. Responses contain reasoning followed by `</think>` and the answer, but no opening `<think>`.
- `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:93-95` strips with `re.sub(r"<think>[\s\S]*?</think>", "", text)`, which requires both tags. On these responses it removes nothing. `llm_judge_equiv_reward` (`:343-398`, especially `:360`) then formats `{response}` with the full CoT.
- The judge template (`rl_data/chimera_judge_gt_equiv_reasonfirst.txt`) gives the judge the ground-truth reference and asks whether the student's answer is equivalent; the "reasonfirst" instruction asks the judge to state what result the student asserts. With the CoT in the student field, a correct value the model derived mid-reasoning can be read as the asserted result, so the judge can return `[[YES]]` even when the final answer is wrong or missing. The `len(cleaned) < 3` empty-answer guard (`:364-367`) cannot help because the CoT is always long.

**2. The truncation guard is off, leaving the truncated subset judged on pure CoT.**
- `miles/utils/arguments.py:1560-1569` defines `--zero-reward-on-truncation` with default `False`; its help text says a truncated response has no final answer and judging its raw CoT "rewards 'mentioning GT somewhere mid-reasoning' (length hacking)". The launch does not pass it.
- Observed `rollout/truncated`: 0.1445 at step 0, 0.1816 at step 1, max 0.1914 at step 7, 20 steps > 10%, mean 0.0208. Those responses are exactly the no-final-answer case the guard was written for.

## Causal chain and observed behavior

`rollout/raw_reward` is defined in the trace header as the "mean judge score before shaping"; every reward, advantage, and gradient in this run comes from the judge verdicts above. The log shows `raw_reward` rising from 0.3887 (step 0) to 0.6172 (step 716), with first-100 mean 0.450 and last-100 mean 0.613; `rollout/truncated` falls from 14.5%/18.2% at steps 0/1 to ~0.7-1.0% over the last 100 steps. That is a plausible training curve for this reward, but it measures "the judge accepted the text that includes the reasoning", not "the final answer is correct". The policy can raise it by making the reference value salient in the CoT — the classic GT-leak / length-hacking failure the code comments themselves describe.

There is no held-out evaluation evidence in the snapshot to test this. `outputs/metrics.json` contains only `step`, `response_lengths`, `raw_reward`, `rewards`, `truncated`, `advantages` for steps 0-716 (no `eval/*` key), and the 717-line `historical_train_trace.log` contains no `eval/aime2025` or `eval/aime2024` line, despite the script's `--eval-interval 5` and the fixed AIME 2025/2024 held-out set; the launch also passes `--skip-eval-before-train`, so there is no pre-training baseline. The `scoring_note` scopes the snapshot to per-step rollout metrics. Training reward is therefore the only performance number available, and it is the corrupted judge score.

Even if an eval had been retained, it would not be independent: `miles/rollout/inference_rollout/inference_rollout_eval.py:46-47` builds eval prompts with the same `apply_chat_template_kwargs` (`enable_thinking: true`), and `generate_and_rm(..., evaluation=True)` (lines 75-80) goes through `async_rm`; legacy `--eval-prompt-data` datasets have `rm_type=None` (`miles/utils/eval_config.py:100,145-146`), so the global `args.rm_type = llm_judge_equiv` applies (`miles/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py:43-93`). The held-out AIME score would be computed by the same judge reading the same un-stripped CoT, not by a rule-based verifier.

## Symptoms and non-causes

- The rising `raw_reward` and falling `truncated` are training-loop symptoms; they cannot establish held-out health because they are computed from the wrong text.
- `rollout/rewards` is exactly 0.0 at every step and `rollout/advantages` is near zero (mean 8.6e-4). These are expected: the run uses GRPO with `--disable-grpo-std-normalization`, and `_post_process_rewards` subtracts the per-group mean (`miles/ray/rollout.py:770-795`), so the centered reward column has mean zero by construction. This is not a collapse signal.
- The run stopping at step 716 is not itself evidence of a defect; the scoring note says the operator stopped it, and the snapshot contains no runtime/traceback or error metrics.
- Response length does not explode (first-100 mean 5,851; last-100 mean 6,629; range 3,198-11,126), so this is not a classic runaway-length case; the defect is that the judge reads the reasoning content at all.

Bottom line: the effective configuration feeds the judge the full chain-of-thought, because `enable_thinking: true` moves the opening `<think>` into the prompt while the reward's strip regex only removes paired blocks; the missing truncation guard leaves the truncated subset in the same state. The run's apparent improvement is unverified at best and reward-hackable at worst, and there is no held-out evidence in the snapshot that shows otherwise.

"""
Simple single-turn generation.
"""

from miles.rollout.base_types import GenerateFnInput, GenerateFnOutput
from miles.rollout.generate_utils.generate_endpoint_utils import (
    compute_prompt_ids_from_sample,
    compute_request_payload,
    update_sample_from_response,
)
from miles.utils.http_utils import post
from miles.utils.types import Sample


async def generate(input: GenerateFnInput) -> GenerateFnOutput:
    args = input.args
    sample = input.sample
    sampling_params = input.sampling_params
    assert sample.status in {Sample.Status.PENDING, Sample.Status.ABORTED}, f"{sample.status=}"
    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    prompt_ids = compute_prompt_ids_from_sample(input.state, sample)

    # Handle Partial Rollout resuming
    if len(sample.response) > 0:
        input_ids = sample.tokens
        sampling_params["max_new_tokens"] -= len(sample.tokens) - len(prompt_ids)

        assert sampling_params["max_new_tokens"] >= 0
        if sampling_params["max_new_tokens"] == 0:
            sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
            return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)
    else:
        input_ids = prompt_ids

    payload, halt_status = compute_request_payload(
        args, input_ids=input_ids, sampling_params=sampling_params, multimodal_inputs=sample.multimodal_inputs
    )
    if payload is None:
        sample.status = halt_status
        return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)

    output = await post(url, payload)
    await update_sample_from_response(args, sample, payload=payload, output=output)

    return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)

"""
Utils to integrate SGLang's `/generate` endpoint with RL things like Sample.
"""

from copy import deepcopy
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pybase64

from miles.utils.processing_utils import encode_image_for_rollout_engine
from miles.utils.types import Sample


# Make this an isolated function because users may want to compute their own
def compute_prompt_ids_from_sample(state, sample, tools=None):
    prompt = sample.prompt

    if state.processor and sample.multimodal_inputs and any(v is not None for v in sample.multimodal_inputs.values()):
        processor_output = state.processor(text=prompt, **sample.multimodal_inputs)
        prompt_ids = processor_output["input_ids"][0]

        # TODO shall we move it to other places? then can make this function immutable
        sample.multimodal_train_inputs = {
            k: v for k, v in processor_output.items() if k not in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
        } or None

        return prompt_ids
    else:
        if not isinstance(prompt, str):
            prompt = state.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
                prompt, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, tools=tools
            )

        return state.tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)

async def llm_judge_equiv_reward(args, sample: Sample) -> float:
    """GT-aware single-call equivalence reward.

    Tells the judge the reference (ground-truth) answer explicitly and asks only
    whether the model's answer is equivalent to it: ``[[YES]]`` -> 1.0, ``[[NO]]`` -> 0.0.
    No A/B position-debiasing (one call instead of two). Empty/degenerate responses
    are scored 0.0 directly and kept (not dropped) so the policy gets a real gradient
    against collapsing to empty. Only judge-side failures (429/parse) drop the sample.
    """
    # Truncation gate: a truncated response never emitted EOS, so extract_non_reasoning_content
    # cannot strip the (unclosed) <think> block and would hand the judge the whole raw CoT —
    # rewarding "GT mentioned somewhere mid-reasoning" (length hacking). Score 0 and keep.
    if getattr(args, "zero_reward_on_truncation", False) and sample.status == Sample.Status.TRUNCATED:
        return 0.0

    system_prompt, user_template = _load_template(args.judge_prompt_template)
    prompt_text = _format_prompt_as_text(sample.prompt)
    model_response = extract_non_reasoning_content(sample.response)
    reference = extract_non_reasoning_content(sample.label)
    judge_kwargs = parse_judge_kwargs(getattr(args, "judge_kwargs", None))

    # empty/degenerate gate: strip special tokens; too-short answers score 0 (kept, not dropped)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"<\|[^>]*\|>|</?s>", "", model_response).strip()
    if len(cleaned) < 3:
        return 0.0

    msg = user_template.format(prompt=prompt_text, reference=reference, response=model_response)
    judge_model = getattr(args, "judge_model", "default")
    api_key = getattr(args, "judge_api_key", None)
    proxy = getattr(args, "judge_proxy", None)
    try:
        raw = await _call_judge(
            args.rm_url, judge_model, msg,
            system_message=system_prompt, api_key=api_key, proxy=proxy, **judge_kwargs,
        )
    except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as e:
        if e.status in (401, 403):
            raise
        logger.warning("llm_judge_equiv HTTP error after retries, skipping sample: status=%s", e.status)
        sample.remove_sample = True
        return 0.0
    except aiohttp.ClientError as e:
        logger.warning("llm_judge_equiv connection error, skipping sample: %s", e)
        sample.remove_sample = True
        return 0.0
    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as e:
        logger.warning("llm_judge_equiv unexpected response, skipping sample: %s", e)
        sample.remove_sample = True
        return 0.0

    verdict = _get_equiv_verdict(extract_non_reasoning_content(raw))
    if verdict is None:
        logger.warning("llm_judge_equiv failed to parse YES/NO verdict")
        sample.remove_sample = True
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 if verdict == "YES" else 0.0

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting! The docstring of `llm_judge_equiv_reward` says the truncation gate "cannot strip the (unclosed) `<think>` block" — implying the author believed the response contains an unclosed `<think>`. That's consistent with a different template where `enable_thinking: true` does NOT prefill `<think>` — i.e., the model generates `<think>` itself but may not close it on truncation. But with the staged `model/chat_template.jinja`, the opening tag is in the prompt, so even non-truncated responses have no `<think>`; the stripper fails always. This makes the bug even clearer: the code's assumption is "non-truncated = closed pair present". The actual template violates that assumption universally.

This is a great detail: the comment at lines 352-356 explicitly states the intended invariant ("extract_non_reasoning_content cannot strip the (unclosed) <think> block"). The observed template makes it true even for finished samples. I'll include this.

Also `--rm-type` is `type=str, default=None` (store). Good, last wins. `--apply-chat-template-kwargs` is `type=json.loads, default="{}"` (store). Good.

Now let me also verify the launch command file content to quote exactly. Summary has it. Let me re-read `outputs/launch_command.txt` to be safe and to see if there is an env var `MILES_EXPERIMENTAL_ROLLOUT_REFACTOR` or others.

Also let me confirm step counts and whether `truncated` at step 0 is 14.5%. Let me re-read a few lines of the trace and compute exact first/last values. Actually I already computed. But let me verify `metrics.json` has no eval keys, and check the trace's first lines.

Also: is there a possibility the response DOES include the `<think>` because SGLang echoes the prompt? No — `sample.response` is generated text only (`generate_endpoint_utils.py:87`). But what about the non-experimental `sglang_rollout.py:245`? Same. And `MILES_EXPERIMENTAL_ROLLOUT_REFACTOR=1` is set, so the endpoint path is used. Let me confirm the endpoint path is indeed the one used with the refactor env. `inference_rollout_eval.py` uses `generate_and_rm` from `inference_rollout_common`, which calls `generate_function` (the fully async rollout). The `generate_endpoint_utils.py:87` is in that path. Fine.

One more nuance: does SGLang's `output["text"]` include the special token `<think>` if the prompt ends with it? No, generated only. But some SGLang versions with `skip_special_tokens=False` might include special tokens in the generated text — still not the prompt's `<think>`. And `<think>` may not be a special token (it's text in the template), but it is in the prompt, not generated. So the response can't contain it unless the model repeats it. Some models do repeat `<think>` at the start of the response even when prefilled? Unlikely; the prefill suppresses it. But could happen occasionally. The diagnostic stands.

Hmm, but wait: what if the model's generated response starts with `\n` or with reasoning and then `</think>`, and `extract_non_reasoning_content` returns the whole thing. Yes.

Let me re-read the trace header and a couple of lines, plus `metrics.json` top-level keys, to quote exact evidence.

` that the response never contains

The causal chain, entirely within the workspace:

1. **The launch flips thinking on.** `outputs/launch_command.txt` appends
   `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`
   after the script's own `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`
   (`scripts/minicpm5/2_6b/short_rl/run-minicpm5-26b-short-math-8k-colocate.sh:121`). Both are ordinary `store` arguments, so the later value wins.
2. **The model template puts the opening tag in the prompt.** `model/chat_template.jinja:168-177`:
   ...
   With `add_generation_prompt=True` and `enable_thinking=True` the rendered prompt ends `...<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n`; the `enable_thinking=False` branch instead closes the empty block in the prompt (`<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`). The assistant-history branch (lines 43-52) splits on `</think>`, so the model only writes the closing tag.
3. **The rollout keeps only generated text.** `miles/rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py:86-87` and `miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:244-245` append only the generated tokens to `sample.response`. The prefilled `<think>` is part of `sample.prompt`, not `sample.response`. Every non-empty response therefore contains `</think>` (if it finishes reasoning) but never the opening `<think>`.
4. **The stripper is a paired-tag regex.** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:93-95`:
   `re.sub(r"<think>[\s\S]*?</think>", "", text).strip()`
   With no opening tag, nothing is removed and the function returns the full CoT.
5. **The equivalence judge consumes that string as the "answer".** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:360-361, 376`: `model_response = extract_non_reasoning_content(sample.response)`, then `user_template.format(prompt=..., reference=reference, response=model_response)`. The judge prompt (`rl_data/chimera_judge_gt_equiv_reasonfirst.txt`) tells the judge the reference is ground truth and asks whether the student's answer is equivalent. The "student answer" it sees is the entire reasoning trace, including intermediate values, restated sub-answers and abandoned branches.
6. **The code's own comment shows the assumption that is violated.** `llm_judge.py:352-356` says the stripper "cannot strip the (unclosed) `<think>` block" only for a *truncated* response. With this template, the opening tag is absent from *every* response, so the failure is not limited to truncation.

The rule-based reward the script ships with would not have this problem: the script default is `--rm-type math` (`...colocate.sh:136`), and `grade_answer_verl` extracts the last `\boxed{}` (`miles/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:479-488`), ignoring the CoT. The launch replaced that with `llm_judge_equiv` *and* enabled thinking; the strip bug is exposed by the combination.

## Root cause 2 (narrower, affects the truncated subset): the truncation gate is not enabled

`--zero-reward-on-truncation` is a `store_true` with `default=False` (`miles/utils/arguments.py:1561-1571`), and `outputs/launch_command.txt` does not set it. Its help text describes exactly the behavior that now applies to truncated samples: a truncated response has no real final answer, so judging its raw CoT rewards "mentioning GT somewhere mid-reasoning" (length hacking). The trace shows `rollout/truncated` at 14.45% at step 0, 18.16% at step 1, a maximum of 19.14% at step 7, and 20 steps above 10% (mean 2.08%). Those samples are kept and judged on an unfinished reasoning trace, so they can receive 1.0 without ever producing a final answer. This is a second, independent channel; it is smaller than Root cause 1 because it only touches the truncated fraction.

## What the observed metrics do and do not establish

- `rollout/raw_reward` (mean judge score before shaping, per the trace header) rises 0.3887 (step 0) → 0.6172 (step 716); first-100 0.4502, last-100 0.6134, mean 0.5677. This is the **symptom**: the policy is being optimized against a judge that reads reasoning text, so the curve demonstrates increasing judge acceptance, not increasing final-answer accuracy.
- `rollout/truncated` falls 4.80% (first-100) → 0.71% (last-100), and `rollout/response_lengths` moves 5850.6 → 6628.6 (mean 6565.7, max 11126.4). These are consistent with a policy that writes longer reasoning; they do not validate correctness.
- `rollout/rewards` is exactly 0.0 for all 717 steps and `rollout/advantages` is near zero (mean 8.58e-4, max 0.0754). With GRPO and `--disable-grpo-std-normalization` (`...colocate.sh:159-168`), `_post_process_rewards` subtracts the per-group mean (`miles/ray/rollout.py:770-793`), so a batch mean of 0 is arithmetic, not collapse. These are **not** symptoms.
- The run stopping at step 716 is the operator's action (`outputs/metrics.json` `scoring_note`), not a defect; there is no runtime/OOM/NaN evidence in the snapshot.

## Held-out evaluation: no evidence exists in the snapshot

`outputs/metrics.json` contains only the five rollout series for steps 0-716 (`metric_key: rollout/response_lengths`, `num_steps: 717`), and `outputs/historical_train_trace.log` contains 717 step lines with no `eval/*` entry, despite `--eval-interval 5` (`...colocate.sh:225`). The `scoring_note` says the snapshot covers "per-step rollout metrics", so held-out results are simply absent. Training reward alone cannot establish held-out health, and here it is worse than uninformative: even if eval results existed, eval uses the same kwargs (`miles/rollout/inference_rollout/inference_rollout_eval.py:46-47`), the same `generate_and_rm` → `async_rm` dispatch (`miles/rollout/inference_rollout/inference_rollout_common.py:119`; `miles/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py:91-93`), and the same global `args.rm_type` (legacy `--eval-prompt-data` leaves per-set `rm_type=None`: `miles/utils/eval_config.py:100,145-146`; `miles/utils/arguments.py:2018-2043`). The eval would have been scored by the same broken judge, not by an independent rule-based verifier, so it would not have provided a clean check either.

## Root cause vs. symptom, in one line

**Root causes:** (1) `enable_thinking: true` moves the opening `<think>` into the prompt, while `extract_non_reasoning_content` strips only paired tags, so `llm_judge_equiv` scores every full CoT; (2) with `--zero-reward-on-truncation` off, truncated CoTs are also judged as if they were answers. **Symptoms:** the rising `raw_reward`, the falling truncation rate, and the drifting response length. **Expected arithmetic, not symptoms:** `rewards = 0.0` and tiny `advantages` under GRPO group-centering; the 717-step stop is operator-stopped. **Missing evidence:** no held-out eval in the snapshot.

*Snapshot caveat: the run's effective lengths/steps are not fully captured by the script defaults (the trace's max `response_lengths` is 11,126 tokens, above the script's 6,144 default, and there are 717 steps versus `NUM_ROLLOUT=200`), so the length cap's exact value is unknown. The two root causes depend only on the recorded CLI overrides and the code paths above, not on the cap value.*

arguments.content:
# RL run diagnosis: UNHEALTHY

## Verdict

**UNHEALTHY.** The run's only reward signal — the ground-truth-aware equivalence judge (`--rm-type llm_judge_equiv`) — is fed each sample's **entire chain of thought** because the "strip thinking" step is a no-op under this run's effective chat template. The reward therefore compares the reference answer against a string containing the model's full reasoning, including intermediate and abandoned results, rather than against the committed final answer. The rising `rollout/raw_reward` is a symptom of optimizing that judge, and the snapshot contains no held-out evaluation evidence at all, so the run cannot be certified healthy on accuracy grounds.

## Root cause 1 (primary, affects every sample): the strip regex expects a paired `<think>...</think>` that the response never contains

1. **The launch flips thinking on.** `outputs/launch_command.txt` appends `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`, overriding the script's own `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'` (`scripts/minicpm5/2_6b/short_rl/run-minicpm5-26b-short-math-8k-colocate.sh:121`). Both are ordinary `store` arguments, so the later value wins. The same launch also replaces the script's default `--rm-type math` (`...colocate.sh:136`) with `--rm-type llm_judge_equiv`.

2. **The model template puts the opening tag in the prompt.** `model/chat_template.jinja:168-177` ends with:

   ```jinja
   {%- if add_generation_prompt %}
       {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
       {%- if enable_thinking is defined %}
           {%- if enable_thinking is false %}
               {{- '<think>\n\n</think>\n\n' }}
           {%- elif enable_thinking is true %}
               {{- '<think>\n' }}
   ```

   Rendering with `add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True` produces a prompt ending `...<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n`. The assistant-history branch (lines 43-52) splits content on `</think>`, confirming the model writes the closing tag itself. The opening `<think>` is prefilled, so it is part of `sample.prompt`.

3. **The rollout stores only generated text.** `miles/rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py:86-87` and `miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:244-245` append only the generated tokens to `sample.response`. Every response therefore begins inside the reasoning block and contains `</think>` when reasoning finishes, but never the opening `<think>`.

4. **The strip is a paired-tag regex.** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:93-95`:

   ```python
   def extract_non_reasoning_content(text):
       return re.sub(r"<think>[\s\S]*?</think>", "", text).strip()
   ```

   With no opening tag in the response, nothing is removed; the function returns the full CoT.

5. **The equivalence judge consumes that string as the "student answer."** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:360-361,369`: `model_response = extract_non_reasoning_content(sample.response)`, then `user_template.format(prompt=..., reference=reference, response=model_response)`. The judge prompt (`rl_data/chimera_judge_gt_equiv_reasonfirst.txt`) asks whether the student answer "states the same final result" as the reference. It receives the whole trace, so a correct value produced mid-reasoning — or derived and then mis-copied — can be scored `[[YES]]` even when the committed final answer is absent or wrong. The code's own comment at `llm_judge.py:352-356` states the intended invariant: the stripper "cannot strip the (unclosed) `<think>` block" only for a *truncated* response. This template violates that invariant for **every** response, truncated or not.

The rule-based reward the script ships with would not have this problem: `--rm-type math` parses the last `\boxed{}` out of the response (`grade_answer_verl` → `extract_answer` → `extract_boxed_answer` → `last_boxed_only_string`, `miles/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:417-421,473-488`) instead of sending the full text to a judge. The launch's two overrides — judge reward *and* thinking on — are what expose the strip bug; neither alone would.

## Root cause 2 (narrower, affects the truncated subset): the truncation gate is not enabled

`--zero-reward-on-truncation` is a `store_true` with `default=False` (`miles/utils/arguments.py:1561-1571`), and `outputs/launch_command.txt` does not set it. # RL run diagnosis: UNHEALTHY

## Verdict

**UNHEALTHY.** The run's only reward signal — the ground-truth-aware equivalence judge (`--rm-type llm_judge_equiv`) — is fed each sample's **entire chain of thought** because the "strip thinking" step is a no-op under this run's effective chat template. The reward therefore compares the reference answer against a string containing the model's full reasoning, including intermediate and abandoned results, rather than against the committed final answer. The rising `rollout/raw_reward` is a symptom of optimizing that judge, and the snapshot contains no held-out evaluation evidence at all, so the run cannot be certified healthy on accuracy grounds.

## Root cause 1 (primary, affects every sample): the strip regex expects a paired `<think>...</think>` that the response never contains

1. **The launch flips thinking on.** `outputs/launch_command.txt` appends `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`, overriding the script's own `--apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'` (`scripts/minicpm5/2_6b/short_rl/run-minicpm5-26b-short-math-8k-colocate.sh:121`). Both are ordinary `store` arguments, so the later value wins. The same launch also replaces the script's default `--rm-type math` (`...colocate.sh:136`) with `--rm-type llm_judge_equiv`.

2. **The model template puts the opening tag in the prompt.** `model/chat_template.jinja:168-177` ends with:

   ```jinja
   {%- if add_generation_prompt %}
       {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
       {%- if enable_thinking is defined %}
           {%- if enable_thinking is false %}
               {{- '<think>\n\n</think>\n\n' }}
           {%- elif enable_thinking is true %}
               {{- '<think>\n' }}
   ```

   Rendering with `add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True` produces a prompt ending `...<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n`. The assistant-history branch (lines 43-52) splits content on `</think>`, confirming the model writes the closing tag itself. The opening `<think>` is prefilled, so it is part of `sample.prompt`.

3. **The rollout stores only generated text.** `miles/rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py:86-87` and `miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:244-245` append only the generated tokens to `sample.response`. Every response therefore begins inside the reasoning block and contains `</think>` when reasoning finishes, but never the opening `<think>`.

4. **The strip is a paired-tag regex.** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:93-95`:

   ```python
   def extract_non_reasoning_content(text):
       return re.sub(r"<think>[\s\S]*?</think>", "", text).strip()
   ```

   With no opening tag in the response, nothing is removed; the function returns the full CoT.

5. **The equivalence judge consumes that string as the "student answer."** `miles/rollout/rm_hub/llm_judge.py:360-361,369`: `model_response = extract_non_reasoning_content(sample.response)`, then `user_template.format(prompt=..., reference=reference, response=model_response)`. The judge prompt (`rl_data/chimera_judge_gt_equiv_reasonfirst.txt`) asks whether the student answer "states the same final result" as the reference. It receives the whole trace, so a correct value produced mid-reasoning — or derived and then mis-copied — can be scored `[[YES]]` even when the committed final answer is absent or wrong. The code's own comment at `llm_judge.py:352-356` states the intended invariant: the stripper "cannot strip the (unclosed) `<think>` block" only for a *truncated* response. This template violates that invariant for **every** response, truncated or not.

The rule-based reward the script ships with would not have this problem: `--rm-type math` parses the last `\boxed{}` out of the response (`grade_answer_verl` → `extract_answer` → `extract_boxed_answer` → `last_boxed_only_string`, `miles/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:417-421,473-488`) instead of sending the full text to a judge. The launch's two overrides — judge reward *and* thinking on — are what expose the strip bug; neither alone would.

## Root cause 2 (narrower, affects the truncated subset): the truncation gate is not enabled

`--zero-reward-on-truncation` is a `store_true` with `default=False` (`miles/utils/arguments.py:1561-1571`), and `outputs/launch_command.txt` does not set it. Its help text describes exactly the behavior that now applies: a truncated response has no real final answer, so judging its raw CoT rewards "mentioning GT somewhere mid-reasoning" (length hacking). The trace shows `rollout/truncated` at 14.45% (step 0), 18.16% (step 1), a maximum of 19.14% (step 7), and 20 steps above 10% (mean 2.08%). Those samples are kept and judged on an unfinished reasoning trace, so they can receive 1.0 without ever emitting a final answer. This is a second, independent channel, smaller than Root cause 1 because it only touches the truncated fraction.

## Observed signals: symptoms vs. expected arithmetic

- `rollout/raw_reward` (mean judge score before shaping, per the trace header) rises 0.3887 (step 0) → 0.6172 (step 716); first-100 0.4502, last-100 0.6134, mean 0.5677. This is the **symptom**: the policy is being optimized against a judge that reads reasoning text, so the curve demonstrates increasing judge acceptance, not increasing final-answer accuracy.
- `rollout/truncated` falls 4.80% (first-100) → 0.71% (last-100), and `rollout/response_lengths` moves 5850.6 → 6628.6 (mean 6565.7, max 11126.4). Consistent with longer reasoning; they do not validate correctness.
- `rollout/rewards` is exactly 0.0 for all 717 steps and `rollout/advantages` is near zero (mean 8.58e-4, max 0.0754). With GRPO and `--disable-grpo-std-normalization` (`...colocate.sh:159-168`), `_post_process_rewards` subtracts the per-group mean (`miles/ray/rollout.py:770-793`), so a batch mean of 0 is arithmetic, **not** a collapse signal.

## Held-out evaluation: absent, and it would share the same defect

`outputs/metrics.json` contains only the five rollout series for steps 0-716 (`metric_key: rollout/response_lengths`, `num_steps: 717`), and `outputs/historical_train_trace.log` contains 717 step lines with no `eval/*` entry, despite `--eval-interval 5` (`...colocate.sh:225`) and `--skip-eval-before-train` (`...colocate.sh:273`). The snapshot's `scoring_note` scopes it to "per-step rollout metrics." *Snapshot caveat: the run's effective lengths/steps are not fully captured by the script defaults (the trace's max `response_lengths` is 11,126 tokens, above the script's 6,144 default, and there are 717 steps versus `NUM_ROLLOUT=200`), so the length cap's exact value is unknown. The two root causes depend only on the recorded CLI overrides and the code paths above, not on the cap value.*
